items.source_title: A note on passing from a quasi-symmetric function expansion to a Schur function expansion of a symmetric function
items.difficulty_reason: The Vandermonde identity alone does not explain why replacing each fundamental series by its compositional Schur quotient works. The authors antisymmetrize each fundamental summand, locate the first departure from the packed composition, and choose the last two exponents of that block so their shifted exchange cancels while preserving the same fundamental admissibility and first departure. The packed monomial alone contributes the padded bialternant.
items.statement_scope: Original Exercise 138 in degree n in n variables with its full composition index, including the stated extension to a commutative coefficient ring. Source Theorem 1 writes F_alpha for Stanley L_alpha, and p2 defines the padded composition. The alternating identities have integer coefficients and specialize to the stated ring.

proof_spans.label: §2, from Proof of Theorem 1 through “which is what we wanted to prove” before §3. Formulas (6)–(8), first departure block, adjacent shifted exponent exchange, and surviving padded alternant.

context_spans.label: §1, finite n variables and weak compositions; Eq. (1) bialternant, Eq. (2) adjacent straightening, Eq. (3) fundamental function and trailing zero padding.

source_caveats: The original p4 Eq. (8) keeps the tail indexed by i and exchanges the two terminal exponents as (b−1,a+1). The adjacent explanatory displays at p4 bottom and p5 top misprint the spectator tail with a repeated index. Eq. (8), p2 Eq. (2), and the p5 final Schur subscripts specify the actual sign reversal in the author text.
The first display of Eq. (7) restates the sum bounds imprecisely. The finite upper limit n and strict positions are explicit in Eq. (3).
Gessel’s 2019 EJC p4 has a separate first-two-runs coverage gap and is retained separately from this complete Garsia–Remmel proof.
